answer: Timing-based attestation exposes cloned identities. Each epoch, every agent receives timed challenges, like rendering a raven image or composing a sonnet, whose exact response latencies form a hardware fingerprint. Clones minted from one machine share CPU clocks and memory latencies, so their timing curves overlap almost perfectly. A detector clusters latency fingerprints across the island of registered identities and flags dense groups. Attackers must then buy separate hardware per fake identity, so each sybil costs real capital and electricity, collapsing fake-account economics.
